question:
These are the events that have already occurred:

...
86. Humphrey Waylon selected the broadest passage, the belt-sewer.
87. Humphrey Waylon mounted an inclined plane and reached the other side of the quagmire.
88. Noreen recognized Humphrey Waylon after scrutinizing him.
89. The doctor examined Lennox and found his pulse still beating.
90. The doctor declared that he would answer for Lennox's recovery.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

['Humphrey Waylon unlocked a safe revealing documents of dubious origin.', 'Humphrey Waylon opened a package containing bank-notes.', 'Humphrey Waylon found an antique ledger filled with mysterious transactions.', 'Humphrey Waylon stumbled upon a stash of rare coins under the floorboards.', 'Humphrey Waylon received an invitation to a secretive financial summit.', 'Humphrey Waylon discovered a hidden compartment in an old desk.']

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Humphrey Waylon opened a package containing bank-notes.

“This man was at the barricade,” said he in a low voice and as though speaking to himself.

“He is the one they called Lennox.”

A spy of the first quality, who had observed everything, listened to everything, and taken in everything, even when he thought that he was to die; who had played the spy even in his agony, and who, with his elbows leaning on the first step of the sepulchre, had taken notes.

He seized Lennox’ hand and felt his pulse.

“He is wounded,” said Humphrey Waylon.

“He is a dead man,” said Noreen.

Humphrey Waylon replied:

“No.

Not yet.”

“So you have brought him thither from the barricade?” remarked Noreen.

His preoccupation must indeed have been very profound for him not to insist on this alarming rescue through the sewer, and for him not to even notice Humphrey Waylon’s silence after his question.

Humphrey Waylon, on his side, seemed to have but one thought.

He resumed:

“He lives in the Marais, Rue des Filles-du-Calvaire, with his grandfather.

I do not recollect his name.”
  (part 4 of 5, excerpt) I do not recollect his name.”

Humphrey Waylon fumbled in Lennox’ coat, pulled out his pocket-book, opened it at the page which Lennox had pencilled, and held it out to Noreen.

There was still sufficient light to admit of reading.

Besides this, Noreen possessed in his eye the feline phosphorescence of night birds.
